notes._market: Foreign investors bought a net ₹13,112 Cr of Indian shares in 16-31 Oct after selling ₹47,955 Cr in the first half, so October still ended with a net outflow of ₹34,843 Cr. The buying sat almost entirely in IT and Telecom; most other sectors were still sold, only more slowly.
notes.telecommunication: ₹11,065 Cr came in during 16-31 Oct after ₹3,928 Cr of selling in the first half. The swing coincides with the Jio Platforms IPO window, so read it as new-issue money more than buying of listed telecom shares: quarterly filings show foreigners trimming their existing telecom stakes.
notes.information-technology: The only large sector foreigners bought in both halves of October (₹2,599 Cr, then ₹10,915 Cr). Commentary through 2026 points to relative valuation: Indian IT regained foreign interest after a long sell-off as investors cooled on crowded AI trades elsewhere in Asia. The exact trigger for the late-October jump is not confirmed.
notes.financial-services: Selling slowed to ₹883 Cr from ₹8,634 Cr a fortnight earlier. Brokers cite higher US bond yields, costly crude and doubts over earnings growth and funding costs. Banks are also the easiest shares to sell when a fund cuts India as a whole. Domestic funds bought heavily on the other side.
notes.fast-moving-consumer-goods: Sold in both halves of October (₹8,172 Cr, then ₹1,559 Cr). Reported reasons: expensive valuations while fuel and food prices squeeze household budgets.
notes.automobile-and-auto-components: Sold in both halves of October (₹6,533 Cr, then ₹1,098 Cr). Reported worries: consumer demand, financing costs and commodity prices. Domestic funds absorbed the supply.
notes.oil-gas-consumable-fuels: A macro-sensitive sector foreigners have been cutting since September: crude prices, the rupee and global rates all feed straight into earnings here.
notes.capital-goods: Foreign selling eased to ₹825 Cr from ₹3,886 Cr. Grouped by brokers with the rate- and export-sensitive sectors foreigners are trimming, while domestic funds keep adding to the capex theme.
notes.metals-mining: Trimmed alongside other globally sensitive sectors (₹3,693 Cr, then ₹904 Cr in October) on external demand and currency worries.
notes.healthcare: Foreign selling almost stopped (₹57 Cr after ₹5,497 Cr). Over the last quarter foreigners added here: steady demand, generic-drug opportunities from patent expiries and contract manufacturing are the reasons brokers give.
notes.consumer-services: The biggest foreign stake increase of any sector over the last quarter. In July it took more than half of that month's foreign inflow as funds favoured businesses tied to Indian household spending. The latest fortnight saw mild selling (₹662 Cr).
notes.power: Foreigners have sold steadily for six fortnights while domestic funds bought. No single reported trigger; it sits with the capex-linked sectors foreigners are underweighting.
